groups.A: Identity & directory (AD trust, IAM role vs SCP)
groups.B: DNS & edge protection (Resolver endpoints, OAC + custom header on ALB)
groups.C: Read the deciding detail (push vs SMS, IaC, Multi-AZ failover, stateless tiers)

42.keywords: existing Microsoft AD, employees use their Windows password for AWS SSO
42.trap: Creating users in IAM Identity Center ignores the existing AD — Identity Center still needs Directory Service to reach Microsoft AD
42.rule: Existing on-prem Microsoft AD → AWS Directory Service (Managed Microsoft AD + trust) → SSO; don't recreate users.

26.keywords: business units share a production account; developers terminate other units' resources
26.trap: 🔁 An SCP never grants access — the fix is an IAM role with resource-level (tag) permissions in the production account
26.rule: Grant scoped access → IAM role in the target account + resource-level/tag conditions; SCPs only restrict.

17.keywords: VPC must resolve both AWS endpoints and the custom AD domain (Managed Microsoft AD)
17.trap: Inbound endpoint is for on-prem/other networks → VPC; resolving a custom domain FROM the VPC needs an outbound endpoint
17.rule: Route 53 Resolver: queries leaving the VPC → OUTBOUND endpoint + forwarding rule to the domain controllers; inbound = into the VPC.

58.keywords: S3 static + ALB/Fargate dynamic behind CloudFront; block direct access to both origins
58.trap: A NACL can't allow 'CloudFront only' (too many changing IPs); twin options differ only in where the WAF web ACL is attached
58.rule: Private S3 origin → OAC + bucket policy; ALB origin → CloudFront custom header + WAF web ACL on the ALB (not on the distribution).

15.keywords: push notifications to iOS/Android apps, cost-effective, under a minute
15.trap: SNS SMS sends text messages to phone numbers, not push notifications to the app
15.rule: Mobile app push → SNS Mobile Push; read the delivery channel word (push vs SMS vs email).

45.keywords: manage infrastructure as code for CI/CD + CDN
45.trap: Elastic Beanstalk deploys apps but doesn't manage infrastructure as code
45.rule: Infrastructure as code → CloudFormation (or CDK); CDN → CloudFront; CloudWatch is never a CDN.

53.keywords: RDS Multi-AZ primary fails — what happens
53.trap: The IP isn't moved — RDS flips the DNS record
53.rule: RDS Multi-AZ failover → the CNAME is switched to the standby (apps reconnect to the same endpoint).

62.keywords: large unpredictable traffic, millions of reads, web/app/DB tiers, scalable + available
62.trap: Stateful instances can't scale freely; Multi-AZ alone doesn't add read capacity (twin options differ in stateless + cache + replicas)
62.rule: Scale web/app tiers → stateless ASG + ElastiCache for state; DB reads → read replicas, availability → Multi-AZ.
